blocks.x: Real-time fraud decisioning on instant rails — 38% lower fraud losses at a higher approval rate
Identity withheld — A top-10 European retail bank, Banking & Financial Services sector, outcome-linked engagement, blended delivery team. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
Batch fraud scoring could not sit on instant-payment paths; fraud analysts cleared alerts by volume, not judgment.

Customer, transaction and device data lived in four estates; features rebuilt per model with inconsistent lineage. Regulators demanded decision-level explanations; the bank could not reconstruct individual authorizations reliably.

We built the streaming decision hub: Kafka/Flink features at event time, champion-challenger models behind policy layers on Dataq Nexus, and full decision replay with cryptographic logs. Network analytics across accounts and devices added organized-fraud detection, while the model-risk pack was produced as we built — documentation the regulator read directly.

items: the agents ran inside a policy envelope with replay, so autonomy never outran the evidence.
lineage and freshness were design constraints from week one, so the measurement never became the controversy.
the models and retrieval systems were evaluated before anyone trusted them — grounded answers, cited sources, measured quality.

blocks.x: Two things from the top-10 European retail bank program generalize — the governance shape and the gate design. Everything else was estate-specific, and pretending otherwise is how programs waste their first quarter The engagement model here was outcome-linked build-run; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: the same diagnostic baselined in two weeks, and a scoped proposal only if the delta justifies it.
